questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A city within Europe and going with my friends

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information needed upon arrival was easy to find. The tricky part was enrolling in the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of assistance from the Erasmus coordinator at Charles university

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was easy. We used a service for Erasmus studens in Prague. It is expensive, but a easy choice if you know the people you are going to live with.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live in the city. A lot of the dorms are 30-40 mins. away from the "center"

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a old system of a lot of bureaucratic and not clear processes. Also if you have full freedom of choice and want courses outside your own faculty, you will get access later than all the other students, which mean a lot of courses are full when you arrive. Information which I would have loved, before e.g. making my orignial OLA

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On the first day you get a login, then you can enrol by yourself at courses at your own faculty. For courses outside of your faculty, you would need to get approval from the professor and then get the Erasmus coordinator at Charles University to enrol you. You can not do that by yourself.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus coordinator was very helpfull and replied very quick on all my emails. The system is a bit old, but they are very helpfull

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only got two of the courses in originally wanted (I had 6 courses in total), but that doesn't mean I didn't have a lot of very great courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the chaos of getting courses, especially if your plan is to take some courses outside of your own faculty and you are on science Ba. My advice would be to not get to lock on some specific courses, because you are probably not going to get it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was okay, great courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very diffrent, some courses was very laid back, others where more demanding. In general, UCPH has higher expectations of you.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In general the teaching a UCPH is very good. I wouldn't recommend going to Prague if you want a more challenging academic experience than you get back home in Copenhagen. That doesn't mean Charles is not good, it is more of a highschool teaching style.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Cultural Heritage in Prague 1, Fundamental Concepts in Philosophy, Hydrodynamics, Introduction to Intellectual History: Approaches and Methods, Introduction to quantum information theory, Introduction to radioastronomy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would especially recommend Cultural Heritage in Prague. A lot of Erasmus students on the course and a great way to experience and learn about the city. But also Introduction to quantum information theory. If you want a bit of a challenge enrol in Introduction to radioastronomy, it is very intersting, but is usually a courses attended by MA and even PhD's. Fundamental Concepts in Philosophy is also a good introduction to philosophy and one of the "easier" courses I attended.

questions.answer: Food and beer is less expensive than expected, which is nice. With Erasmus+ and SU you can come a long way.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really use thaht

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't know. But i know there are a lot of things.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Again wouldn't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside of Prague, the country is very beautiful especially up north.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Europeans share more culture than I first expected.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with people in your class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not a lot really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their appreciation of good beer ;))

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open to new things. Dont expected to get all the courses you initially wanted and go out and use the city, it is very nice place.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a lot of new friends and getting to know another city

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The course registration.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
